slices.focus: Tasha's cleanup work becomes an official pilot with calendar, referral form, and backup process
slices.summary: Tasha turns her background cleanup work into an actual pilot plan approved by Miriam. Using three months of handwritten attendance sheets, volunteer call logs, and a color-coded spreadsheet she built at home, she presents evidence of how often the team was improvising. The pilot includes a six-month structured grief-group calendar, a standard referral form to fix inconsistent intake, and a backup volunteer list. Tasha feels the shift from patching holes to operational leadership, even without a title change, and the agent helps her plan a one-page scope document, success metrics (fewer coverage scrambles, fewer incomplete referrals), and a request for a standing maintenance block during work hours.

slices.focus: Renee catches Tasha's jaw clenching; Tasha starts dental guard and evening routine
slices.summary: Renee notices Tasha rubbing her jaw during supervision and has her track body symptoms for two weeks, revealing a pattern of nightly jaw clenching and morning tension headaches worsened by the pilot period's stress. Tasha gets a dental guard, starts a stricter evening wind-down (phone across the room, no work notes in bed, lights lowered earlier), and develops a morning check-in to notice whether she woke up clenched. The agent helps her frame the routine as 'minimum viable strictness' — a simple 2-3 step sequence (guard, playlist, book, lights low) that can survive even late work nights rather than collapsing under all-or-nothing thinking.
